o: Reviewing the itemized invoice after each billing period closes
Moving eligible virtual machines to spot pricing for the deepest discount
Deleting unattached disks and idle resources at the end of each month
Estimating spend in advance and tracking usage against budgets
fixes.e: Predictability comes from forecasting expected spend before deployment and then comparing actual usage against budgets as the quarter progresses. Reviewing the invoice after the period closes only explains money already spent, and spot pricing and idle-resource cleanup can lower the bill but make it no easier to forecast, since spot rates and evictions vary.

o: The services and tiers planned for the solution
The resource group structure planned for the deployment
The regions where the resources will run
The management group hierarchy planned for the tenant
The Azure Policy assignments planned for governance
fixes.e: The calculator prices what you intend to deploy: each service, its tier and size, and the region that hosts it, because rates differ by product and location. Resource groups, management groups, and policy assignments organize and govern resources but carry no charge of their own, so the calculator never asks about them.

o: An Azure Monitor metric alert on virtual machine CPU
A Service Health alert scoped to the subscription
An activity log alert on resource deployment operations
A budget with an alert rule in Cost Management
fixes.e: A Cost Management budget fires email alerts at defined thresholds, such as 80 percent of the monthly amount, while leaving every resource running untouched. Azure Monitor metric alerts and activity log alerts watch performance counters and control-plane operations rather than accumulated spend, and Service Health alerts report platform incidents, so none of them can track a monthly cost threshold.

o: All applications are consolidated behind a single hardened network perimeter
Employees must connect through the corporate VPN even when working on site
Every request is verified no matter where it starts
An additional inspection firewall is placed between the office and the internet
fixes.x: A company adopts a Zero Trust model across its corporate offices and remote workforce. What changes in day-to-day security practice?
fixes.e: Zero Trust's verify-explicitly principle authenticates and authorizes every request on all available signals, whether it originates at headquarters or a coffee shop. Mandatory VPNs, consolidated perimeters, and added inspection firewalls all extend trust based on network location, which is exactly the assumption the model abandons.

o: Deploying a landing zone with core networking and identity services
Drafting operational runbooks for the cloud support team
Standardizing resource tagging and cost-governance policies
Building a prioritized digital estate inventory
Defining business justification and expected outcomes
fixes.e: The Strategy and Plan methodologies come first: define the business justification and expected outcomes, then inventory and prioritize the digital estate so a migration backlog exists. Landing zone deployment, tagging and governance standards, and operational runbooks belong to the Ready, Govern, and Manage methodologies that build on an agreed strategy and plan.

o: Assign an Azure Policy that audits resources missing the tag
Export the resource list to CSV and edit the tag column in the spreadsheet
Script the change with Azure PowerShell
Recreate each resource from an ARM template that includes the tag
fixes.x: A new administrator must apply one identical tag to 200 existing resources in a subscription. Which approach suits a change of this size?
fixes.e: A short Azure PowerShell or Azure CLI loop can stamp the same tag on hundreds of resources in one run, and the script can be saved, reviewed, and rerun later. An audit policy only reports resources that lack the tag without adding it, an exported CSV is a read-only snapshot whose edits change nothing in Azure, and recreating 200 resources from templates risks downtime for a simple metadata change.

o: Require an approved client application
Require multi-factor authentication at sign-in
Require the device to be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined
Require the device to be marked as compliant
fixes.x: Administrators should be able to open the Azure portal only from devices that meet the requirements in the organization's Intune device policies. Which Conditional Access access control enforces this requirement?
fixes.e: Intune compliance policies evaluate devices against the organization's requirements and mark passing devices as compliant, and the require-compliant-device grant control admits only devices carrying that status. Requiring a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device verifies how the device is joined to the directory, not whether it satisfies Intune policy, and approved client app and multi-factor authentication constrain the application or the user rather than the device's state.

o: Unused execution credits from busy bursts roll over to offset the next month's bill
Charges pause for the remainder of the month once a preset spending cap is reached
Compute is allocated as events arrive and charges accrue only while executions run
Dedicated worker VMs are deallocated automatically after a configurable idle timeout
fixes.e: On the consumption plan, instances exist only while events are being processed and billing is based on execution count, duration, and memory, so hours of silence generate no compute charges. Automatic deallocation of dedicated worker VMs describes plans that hold reserved infrastructure, and rollover credits and mid-month spending pauses are not part of the consumption billing model.

o: Enforcing multi-factor authentication for every sign-in
Segmenting the environment with least-privilege access for each identity
Requiring complex passwords that rotate on a fixed schedule
Encrypting all traffic that crosses the internal network
fixes.e: Assume breach pairs with segmentation and least privilege so a compromised account unlocks only a narrow slice of the environment instead of the whole estate. Multi-factor authentication and password rotation aim to prevent the credential theft the design already assumes will succeed, and encrypting internal traffic protects data from eavesdropping without restricting where an authenticated intruder can go.
